content.question_text: What is an ArrayList in Java?

core_requirements: A generic class with a type parameter.
It has a dynamically resizable array (can grow/shrink automatically).
acceptable_variations: A resizable array implementation of the List interface.
A generic collection that can expand dynamically.

content.question_text: How does an ArrayList differ from a basic array?

core_requirements: An ArrayList has a dynamic size that can expand or shrink automatically.
A basic array has a fixed size once created.
acceptable_variations: ArrayList is resizable; arrays are fixed length.

content.question_text: Can you use var with the diamond syntax when creating an ArrayList? If so, what type is inferred?

core_requirements: Yes, you can use var with the diamond syntax.
It yields an ArrayList with type Object (ArrayList<Object>).
acceptable_variations: var list = new ArrayList<>(); infers ArrayList<Object>.

content.question_text: What is considered a raw type ArrayList?

core_requirements: An ArrayList without a type parameter (e.g., ArrayList instead of ArrayList<String>).
It behaves like an ArrayList of Object.
acceptable_variations: ArrayList<Object> is essentially the same as the raw type in practice.

content.question_text: How do you add elements to an ArrayList?

core_requirements: Using the .add() method.
acceptable_variations: Call add() on the ArrayList instance.

content.question_text: What happens internally when an ArrayList runs out of space?

core_requirements: ArrayList automatically creates a larger internal array.
It copies all existing elements from the old smaller array to the new larger one.
acceptable_variations: It resizes by allocating a new array and copying elements over.

content.question_text: When you know approximately how many elements you want to store, what can you do to improve performance?

core_requirements: Call .ensureCapacity(x) before filling the ArrayList.
Or pass the initial capacity as an integer parameter to the ArrayList constructor.
acceptable_variations: Set initial capacity in the constructor to avoid frequent resizing.

content.question_text: What is the difference between an ArrayList with a capacity of 100 and a regular array of size 100?

core_requirements: A regular array has 100 slots ready to use immediately.
An ArrayList with capacity 100 has the capacity to hold 100 elements but initially holds no elements (size is 0).
acceptable_variations: Array has pre-allocated slots; ArrayList only has the capacity, not actual elements.

content.question_text: How do you check the current number of elements in an ArrayList?

core_requirements: Using the .size() method.
acceptable_variations: Call size() on the ArrayList instance.

content.question_text: When you are sure an ArrayList is at its permanent size (no more elements will be added), what can you do to reduce memory usage?

core_requirements: You can call the .trimToSize() method.
acceptable_variations: Use trimToSize() to free excess capacity.

content.question_text: What exactly does the trimToSize() method do?

core_requirements: It adjusts the internal array's capacity to exactly match the current number of elements.
This reduces memory usage by freeing unused capacity.
acceptable_variations: Trims the capacity to the current size.
Shrinks the backing array to fit the exact number of stored elements.

content.question_text: Why can't you use the [] array indexing operator with ArrayLists?

core_requirements: Java does not support operator overloading.
ArrayLists use methods like .get(index) and .set(index, element) instead.
acceptable_variations: [] is reserved for arrays only; ArrayList uses get() and set().
